definitions.explanation: Something made or created by oneself. Used for anything from computers built from parts, to poems or songs one has written, to food one has grown. Emphasizes that the creator and the user/owner are the same person.

examples.japanese: {自作|じさく}のパソコンを{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: I'm using a computer I built myself.

examples.japanese: {自作|じさく}の{曲|きょく}をネットで{公開|こうかい}した。
examples.english: I posted a song I wrote myself online.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}が{自作|じさく}した{棚|たな}は{既製品|きせいひん}よりもしっかりしている。
examples.english: The shelf my friend built himself is sturdier than store-bought ones.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a noun modifier with の ({自作|じさく}のパソコン) or as a suru-verb ({自作|じさく}する = to make/build oneself). Very common in hobbies and tech culture: {自作|じさく}PC (DIY/custom-built PC) is a major hobby in Japan.

Compared to {手作|てづく}り (handmade), {自作|じさく} emphasizes that you made it yourself (self as creator), while {手作|てづく}り emphasizes the handcrafted method. Compared to {自家製|じかせい} (homemade, house-made), {自作|じさく} focuses on personal creation while {自家製|じかせい} focuses on being made at home or in-house.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自作|じさく}PC: custom-built PC
- {自作|じさく}の{曲|きょく}: a song one wrote
- {自作|じさく}{自演|じえん}: staging one's own work (also: creating a problem and pretending to solve it)
- {自作|じさく}の{野菜|やさい}: vegetables one grew oneself
